Specimen ontology rules, version 2.0. Each rule names its Darwin Core term and how it is checked.
- one_collecting_event: A specimen has one collecting event. When two of its labels write different text for one of its fields, a collecting date or a place among them, an answer that settles the field on one label's text is refused unless a source confirms each label's text as the same place or name. (Darwin Core: Event: eventDate; dcterms:Location: locality; checked by code.)
- place_within_settled_places: Below the country, a place candidate settles only when its source names its parents. When a country is settled for its reading, the place lies in it; when a province is, a county or a city lies in that province; and a county is never the settled province itself. When the country has no value settled for the reading, or, for a county or a city, the province its reading writes has no settled value, an exact match still settles when that larger place can be derived from it later: the reading writes no text for it, writes the candidate's own misfiled text there, or writes text already settled at a level between them; for the country, also when the gazetteers confirm the record's every text for it as the candidate's parent; for a province, only when the candidate's source names two parents or more. A near spelling settles only when every larger place its reading writes is one of its parents. A place that does not fit is refused when its value is applied. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county, municipality; checked by code.)
- place_chain: The places form one chain, country > province or state > county > city. A settled value outside the chain settled above it is marked for a person, including what the refusal at apply time lets pass (a settled Coles County, then an exact "Chicago" under Illinois), and so is a chain that derivation fills when it breaks the chain. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county, municipality; not yet checked.)
- date_order: The collecting date is on or before the determination date; the same day is allowed. Dates written at different precisions compare on the parts both have ("1946" and "1946-09-06" agree). A determination dated before the collecting date is marked for a person, both dates listed. (Darwin Core: eventDate, dateIdentified; not yet checked.)
- day_month_order: A numeric date in which no part over 12 tells the day from the month, and whose two orders give two different dates, reads two ways: the date check settles neither reading, and an answer that lists both leaves the field ambiguous, a conflict with both readings for a person. When both orders give one date (5-5-48), it settles. (Darwin Core: eventDate, dateIdentified; checked by code.)
- code_is_no_date: A slide or preparation code is never a date, nor is any part of it: text that stands inside a longer hyphen-joined code in any reading is no date. (Darwin Core: ours: no Darwin Core term fits a code; eventDate; checked by code.)
- label_type_routing: A label's type (locality, determination, code) sends its units to the experts of its fields first and never keeps a field's expert from a unit: a determination label that writes a locality reaches the locality expert. (Darwin Core: ours: no Darwin Core term fits a label; not yet checked.)
- elevation_unit_feet: An elevation whose cleared text writes no unit is read as feet only when (a) at least one reader wrote the foot mark or "ft" at this unit, (b) the number read as metres is above the highest point of the specimen's country, which is cleared, not marked (the highest-point table), and (c) the number read as feet is possible (16000 with a mark is not, in the Philippines). When all hold, the elevation settles in feet, cleared, its reason "Basis: inferred, rule elevation_unit_feet". Without (a) the field is unresolved: magnitude alone never decides; so it is when (b) or (c) fails or the country is marked. Terrain takes no part while the owner's decision D5 is held. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; not yet checked.)
- elevation_needs_a_unit: An answer that settles an elevation field on a number that one of its readings writes with no unit is refused: a unit is never guessed from the magnitude, the place or a map. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- elevation_unit_decides_field: An answer that settles an elevation field on a number that one of its readings writes in the other unit is refused; the other unit's fields come from the conversion. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- place_parents_derived: Upward derivation: a country, a province or state, or a county the label leaves without a value takes, derived, the parent that the source of a settled place below it names at that level (a province's source names its country; a county's, its province and country; a city's, its county, province and country), when every settled place that names a parent there names the same one. A county comes from a city only when the city's source names three parents or more, and a province from a county only when the county's names two or more. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county; checked by code.)
- elevation_conversion: One stated elevation fills both ends of its unit, and, when the label states nothing in the other unit, the other unit's fields hold its exact conversion, feet to metres or metres to feet, at 1 ft = 0.3048 m, to the hundredth. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- end_date_from_one_date: When the label states one collecting date, the collection ends on the day it began: Date Visited To takes Date Visited From's date, at its precision. A written range keeps both its ends as written. (Darwin Core: eventDate; checked by code.)
- precise_location_extent: Precise Location is the label's locality as written: every line of its locality text, with its line breaks, the higher places and an elevation written among those lines included. It is never cut to the first line, and a label whose locality names nothing finer than its town still has a Precise Location: those lines as written. (Darwin Core: verbatimLocality; not yet checked.)

Not rules:
- taxon_regional_occurrence: A taxon's regional occurrence is not a rule: that an authority records no occurrence of a taxon in a region does not make it impossible there, and no check uses occurrence while the owner's decision D4 is held. (Darwin Core: scientificName; dcterms:Location.)
